# colorgen

> CLI tool that extracts colors from an image and generates terminal colorschemes for kitty, AwesomeWM, Waybar, dunst and rofi.

colorgen reads an image, picks a palette and writes config files for the tools listed above. These docs cover installation, the CLI, the Python API and a short FAQ.

## Docs

- [Terminal colorscheme generator from images](https://docs.colorgen.piotrkrzysztof.dev/): colorgen is a Python command line tool that pulls dominant colors from an image and writes terminal colorschemes for kitty, AwesomeWM, Waybar, dunst and rofi.
- [Install colorgen with pip or from source](https://docs.colorgen.piotrkrzysztof.dev/installation/): Install colorgen from PyPI with pip, or from source with Poetry. Needs Python 3.12 or 3.13 and is aimed at Linux. Also covers the command not found error.
- [Quick start: preview and apply a colorscheme](https://docs.colorgen.piotrkrzysztof.dev/quickstart/): Quick start for colorgen: preview an image palette, write a kitty config, apply it, target several tools at once, and pick a dark or light theme from the CLI.
- [CLI reference: colorgen options and examples](https://docs.colorgen.piotrkrzysztof.dev/usage/cli/): Reference for the colorgen command line: the image argument, flags for config targets, theme, apply and preview, examples, output paths and how apply works.
- [Python API: extract palettes and write configs](https://docs.colorgen.piotrkrzysztof.dev/usage/api/): Use colorgen from Python: extract a 19-color palette with Extractor, write and apply a kitty config with KittyGen, or run many targets with GenerationManager.
- [colorgen FAQ: palette, formats and config files](https://docs.colorgen.piotrkrzysztof.dev/faq/): Answers about colorgen: the 19-color palette, how colors are picked, which images work, whether it overwrites configs and how to add support for another tool.

## Optional
